doc.title: Alcide "Slow Drag" Pavageau and Lawrence Marrero Interview, 1957-09-01

title: Marrero's wrist action and his injured finger
summary: Allen asks about Marrero's wrist work; Marrero explains his mattress-factory accident left him unable to use his first finger, so he holds the pick differently.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: Excuse me. Any bill? Yeah, he's a good bill.
He's a good bill. He's a good bill. I'd like to see your wrist work when you travel over that banjo.
Well I'll tell you, before the wrist work, I ain't got much wrist work.
Well how are you doing it? Because nothing has been giving me bits too. What's the church?
The trombone, yeah. It all depends on the wrist. It all depends on the wrist. It all depends on the wrist. It all depends on the wrist. Wow. It goes to the trombone.
It goes to the trombone. You're not using the forefinger to hold the pick at all, you leave that out, don't you?

Well I'll tell you, I told you to tell your butt. You see I used to be a mattress maker one time. The sudden mattress coming in and my finger cut the machine and gin be cutting gin. That's why I said I don't use this finger much. I see. I used this finger here. I wish I could use this finger. I didn't know it, Lars, all the years.
I know you didn't know it. Nobody knew it.
I know nobody knew it. Well anyway this is just as good except that you're going to hurt your finger.
That one got cut? See it man?
Oh yeah. That finger is broken.
That finger is broken, that steel tacks the finger all together. The first finger. I can't glue the hand tight. I can't glue the hand tight. I see.
That's why you do this. Otherwise this is just as good. Yes. I see.
So you hold the pick most of the second and then? That's right, that's right. I don't hear that before.
I just look at your wrist. Well what is going to do you play?
